summary: Timothy Lubin is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from Columbia University by 1994. He taught Christian K. Wedemeyer and held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2020).
Tina Rasmussen works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teacher Pa-Auk Sayadaw and completed her MA under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Tissa Rajapatirana is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the Australian National University (1966–1974) under Jan Willem de Jong. He later taught at the university's Department of South Asian and Buddhist Studies (attested 1988).
Tiziana Pontillo is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at the University of Cagliari in 2016 and held a post there in 2022.
Todd A. Gibson is a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar. He completed his PhD at Indiana University (attested 1991), where he studied under György Kara.

Todd Thornton Lewis is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at Columbia University under numerous scholars, including Margaret Mead and Alex Wayman. He held professorships at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 1996, 2016–2017).

Tokan Tada was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Sera Monastery (1913–1923). He served as a lecturer at Tohoku University (~1931–1945) and held a post at the University of Tokyo (~1946–1960).
Tokio Takata is a scholar of Sinology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kyoto University from ~1967 to 1976 and later held a post there from ~1980 to 2014.
Tokugen Sakai was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University from ~1934 to 1937. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from ~1955 to 1982.

Tokuno Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fukui Prefectural Normal School, Otani University, and under Gaju Ikehara. He held posts at Fukui Prefectural Normal School (1879), Fukui Chugakko (1879–1882), and Toyo University (~1898–1904).

Tokuryu Yamauchi was a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1916–1919). He later held posts at Kyoto University of Education (~1949–1953), Kyoto Institute of Technology (~1953–1959), and Ryukoku University (~1959–1966).

Tom J. F. Tillemans is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held a post as Emeritus Professor at the University of Lausanne (attested 1987–2018) and served as the Visiting Numata Chair at the University of Calgary.

Tomoko Masuzawa is a religious studies and history scholar who studied at International Christian University, UC Santa Barbara (~1977–1985), and Yale. She held faculty posts at UNC Chapel Hill (~1988–2000) and the University of Michigan (1999, ~2000).
Tomoyasu Oshima is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Toshifumi Goto (attested 2012). He held a post as a part-time lecturer at Kyoto University (attested 2012).
Tomoyuki Komine is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. He also held an appointment there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2015).

Tomoyuki Uno is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He was affiliated with Hiroshima University and the JSPS in 1998, and served as an associate professor at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2000–2006).

Tomy Augustine is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He earned a master's at the University of Madras, completed a PhD at Banaras Hindu University under Munni K. Agrawal, and held a post at Salesian College (attested 2008).

Toni Huber is a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison and William Sax. He held professorships at Victoria University of Wellington (attested 2000) and Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 2006–2008).

Tony K. Stewart is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at Western Kentucky University (~1972–1976). He held academic posts at North Carolina State University (~1986–2011) and Vanderbilt University (~2011).

Torkel Brekke is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He earned an MPhil at the University of Oslo (~1993–1995) and a doctorate at Oxford under Richard Gombrich (1996–1999), later holding posts at Oxford (1998) and Oslo (~2001).
